findings.reason: _compact_gate (line 128) keeps only 'code' and 'gate_id', but soak/evidence.py:198-213 observed_faults requires the post-restart authority_snapshot owner_gate to match ('gate_id','code','task_id','reason') against the live gate, and line 199 already forces gate['reason'] to be truthy. Trigger: any fault case whose disposition is 'owner_gate'. Verified by executing _compact_gate: task_id and reason are dropped, so all(...) is always False, after_restart is always empty, len(after_restart)<3 continues, and observed_faults returns no disposition for that fault. Impact: qualification always reports missing_fault_dispositions for the owner_gate half of the 15 cases, so no live run can ever reach ACCEPT; violates contract item 4 ('Compact observations retain the fields used by verifiers'). Fix: include bounded task_id and a truncated reason in _compact_gate (or compare only retained fields plus the row-level task_id in observed_faults), and add a regression asserting observed_faults accepts a compacted snapshot.

Line 1128 maps a current-task planner state 'recovery_required' to authority lifecycle_state 'RECOVERY_REQUIRED' (line 1021 does the same for a recovery_required review obligation), but RECOVERY_REQUIRED is absent from watchdog.ACTIVE_LIFECYCLE_STATES and LIFECYCLE_OVERRIDE_FAMILY (core/watchdog.py:45-72), so evaluate_stall sets monitored=False/breached=False (watchdog.py:913) and no diagnosis or bounded recovery ever runs; the PLANNING_RECOVERY_EXHAUSTED promotion at lines 1129-1137 is circular because it requires owner_store.latest_gate() plus a watchdog planning_recovery_problems entry that only the never-triggered watchdog recovery can create, and watchdog.py:2841 hard-requires current_lifecycle=='PLAN_FAILED'. Trigger: a current-task Planner reaching state 'recovery_required' (set at core/ai_planner.py:477, one of the two states the diagnosis observed across the 15 cases) with no pre-existing owner gate. Impact: D04 is not fixed for this branch - the terminal role failure is neither Watchdog-recoverable nor a stable authority gate, so the case silently stalls to its 1200 s timeout exactly as in the failed run, and test_current_failed_planner_is_not_hidden_by_pending_design gives false confidence because it only asserts the projected label. Fix: add RECOVERY_REQUIRED to ACTIVE_LIFECYCLE_STATES and LIFECYCLE_OVERRIDE_FAMILY (PLANNING/REVIEWING family), or open a durable authority owner_gate directly for the current-task recovery_required terminal, with a test asserting evaluate_stall reports monitored=True and breaches.

The segmented store (lines 10-12: SEGMENT_BYTES 8 MiB, MAX_SEGMENTS 16, MAX_TOTAL_BYTES 128 MiB; lines 63-68) has no retention, archival or eviction path, and on exhaustion _append_rows raises, which daemon.py:574-580 turns into transition_executor.record_observation_failure (line 1211) opening RELIABILITY_OBSERVATION_UNAVAILABLE with lifecycle_state='OWNER_GATE' for every project in the tick summary (_snapshot_map), halting all lifecycle progress. Trigger: the canonical runtime already holds runtime/reliability/invariant-observations.jsonl at 67,228,405 bytes, which the first tick under this code seals as segment 000001 and never evicts, permanently consuming ~50% of MAX_TOTAL_BYTES; at the measured 2,253 bytes/tick/project that leaves about 20 days at the 60 s default interval and about 3.4 days at the soak's 5 s interval. Impact: a guaranteed future control-plane halt for every project, and the gate is not operator-clearable - approving it re-gates on the next tick because the append still fails, while manually deleting files makes _segments raise 'missing or unindexed observation segment' unless the index is repaired in lockstep. Fix: scope the bounded store and its gate to an open reliability/soak measurement run, or archive sealed segments that fall outside any open measurement window, and document/implement a consistent index+segment repair path so the gate reflects an actual at-risk measurement rather than cumulative age.

read_observations re-reads, SHA-256s and JSON-parses the entire retained history while holding the inter-process observations.lock that _append_rows needs, and the supervisor calls it three times per 5 s poll (evidence.observed_hard_zeros, reliability_telemetry:737, verification_sources.continuous_escape_metric). Lock hold time grows linearly with the run; InterProcessFileLock raises TimeoutError after 30 s, which the daemon converts into the new OWNER_GATE, and delayed appends can break continuous_escape_metric's <=30 s gap requirement - the same class of defect as D06's 153 s observation gap. Prefer segment-cached or time-bounded reads.

observed_hard_zeros (line 106) and verification_sources.continuous_escape_metric (line 83) still report coverage 'source' as the single active invariant-observations.jsonl, which no longer names the segmented store the value was actually derived from; the evidence label understates the real source set.

compute_run_duration line 208 compares psutil create_time() by exact float equality. On Linux psutil derives create_time from /proc/stat btime, which shifts with wall-clock corrections, so a normal NTP step would be reported as supervisor_process_discontinuity - the same false-reboot class as D01. Windows (the measurement platform) uses absolute GetProcessTimes and is unaffected, so this is a portability note rather than a live blocker. Also line 247 calls _current_boot_id() once per segment inside the loop, issuing an ntdll query per iteration; hoist it above the loop.

parent_expired runs on every tick of every daemon and is called at daemon.py:830 outside the tick try, so a ValueError from missing or invalid permit artifacts kills the daemon without writing the normal 'stopped' record or interrupting owned Broker dispatches. It also validates both permits against config.REPO_ROOT rather than the parent permit's canonical_repo_path, which couples the guard to the real repository root and makes it unusable in a self-contained fixture. Catch and record the guard failure, and anchor validation to the parent permit's declared canonical repo.

The new pending-review fence at line 1786 exempts only source_kind=='remediation', so an explicit owner start (_advance_owner_start, source_kind='owner_start') is refused whenever a completed execution still carries review_state:'pending' for the same task - and review_state is only ever written as 'pending' (lines 2140, 2434), draining solely via a same-task handoff/settled barrier. Owners retain retry/remediation, but there is no explicit-owner override for the barrier. Separately, the latest-plan selection at line 1125 sorts on row.get('started_at') or row.get('completed_at') or '', so a row carrying only completed_at can outrank a newer in-progress plan.

The resolve_successor preflight added at lines 155-161 runs once at generation time against the already-checked-out working tree, so it proves the native resolver accepts the generated roadmap but does not re-verify bytes after a fresh clone/worktree checkout or after successor activation, which is the literal wording of contract item 6 ('including checkout bytes'). The accepted kind set also admits 'absent'/'unlisted' alongside a matching successor id, which is looser than needed. Consider re-running the resolver from a throwaway clone of the generated commit.

The heterogeneous-failover candidate filter at lines 1717-1731 ignores the roles/qualities fields that aibroker_subprocess.resource_snapshot returns, so a candidate ineligible for the reviewer role at the required quality can still satisfy the 'any remaining candidate' test and consume one of the bounded max_attempts before Broker refuses it. Bounded and quality/independence constraints are preserved, so this only wastes an attempt; filtering candidates by declared dispatch roles/qualities would make the budget more useful.

observed_faults requires len(after_restart) >= 3 post-restart authority_snapshot rows, while live_faults._run_case only guarantees 'time.monotonic() - stable_since >= 15.' after self._restart() at a 5 s daemon tick cadence, checked on a 5 s poll. This margin was unreachable before B1 (the identity comparison always failed, so the count was always 0) and becomes the binding constraint now that the correlation works: with a daemon tick that itself takes several seconds the effective cadence stretches and only 2 snapshots may land before _finish, so a correct owner_gate disposition is recorded by the driver and then rejected by the verifier as missing_fault_dispositions. It fails closed (no false acceptance) but can cost a 12-hour measurement. Cheap bounded fix: make the driver require a counted number of observed post-restart snapshots for the same compact gate identity (or widen the post-restart window to ~45 s) rather than relying on elapsed seconds matching the tick interval.

The PrefetchParameters successful-boot BootId DWORD is published by the boot-trace/prefetcher path shortly after the session starts rather than atomically at boot, so a run opened inside that early window can observe the counter advance mid-run and report a false system_boot_discontinuity (exit 4) - the same availability class as the original D01 failure, though in the fail-closed direction. Verified the value reads cleanly here (55, REG_DWORD). Conversely, if the prefetcher is disabled the counter can stop advancing, but a real reboot is still caught independently by monotonic_rollback_observed, the >10 s wall/monotonic divergence fence, the supervisor PID/create-time check, and run_soak_supervisor's refusal to let a replacement supervisor reuse an existing run, so there is no soundness hole. Bounded mitigation: sample the counter twice at open_soak_run, or require a minimum system uptime before a measurement may open.

record_post_tick_observations raises ObservationFailure on the first failing run inside the per-run loop, so any remaining open v2 runs in the same runtime silently receive no rows for that tick and are not identified in the gate. In practice each runtime root holds one open measurement (the supervisor opens one for the primary; each fault case uses its own runtime root), and the resulting coverage gap fails closed at verification, so this is a robustness refinement rather than a live defect. Collect per-run failures and gate each affected project instead of aborting the loop.

Only failures raised inside the per-run try are wrapped as ObservationFailure with project_ids. Errors raised earlier in record_post_tick_observations - a corrupt reliability/runs.jsonl, a runs.lock TimeoutError, or a failure inside _observation_rows - propagate as plain ValueError/OSError, so record_observation_failure sees no project_ids and still opens RELIABILITY_OBSERVATION_UNAVAILABLE for every project in the tick summary. These causes are genuinely unattributable, so gating broadly is defensible fail-closed behaviour; attaching the set of measured project ids from the registry read would keep the blast radius inside actual measurements.

Dropping the 'repo_task != owner_task' condition from the blocked_obligations branch is contract-mandated (diagnosis D04 requires covering the same-task blocked review obligation), but NEXT_TASK_WITHOUT_HANDOFF is never auto-cleared: once set, the gate-first branch keeps lifecycle_state at OWNER_GATE even after the existing reopen_handoff path restores a transiently blocked actuation (transient dirty worktree or stale anchor) to 'handoff'. A self-healing condition therefore becomes a permanent gate needing owner approval, and in a soak that approval would itself break the lifecycle_repair hard zero. Bounded fix: clear this specific gate when no blocked obligation remains for the current task, or restrict it to actuation_state values that cannot be reopened.

Carried over from R1 and not part of this delta: parent_expired validates both the case and parent permits against config.REPO_ROOT rather than the parent permit's declared canonical_repo_path, coupling the guard to the real repository root. The related R1 note is otherwise addressed - daemon.py now converts a guard error into a normal bounded shutdown that writes daemon.json with reason 'soak_parent_guard_unavailable' and the error type, and the canonical runtime holds no soak-parent-owner.json so the production daemon is unaffected.

Carried over from R1 and unchanged in this delta: the heterogeneous-failover candidate test ignores the roles/qualities fields returned by resource_snapshot, so a candidate ineligible for the reviewer role at the required quality can satisfy the 'any remaining candidate' check and consume one of the bounded max_attempts before Broker refuses it. The finite budget, high quality and provider independence are preserved, so the only cost is a wasted attempt.
